value.title: Standard Operating Procedure: Managing Flight Delays Exceeding Three Hours for B2B Bookings
value.purpose: Define a standardized, prioritized workflow for identifying travel agent bookings affected by flight delays exceeding three hours, evaluating downstream connection risks, and communicating rebooking or refund options to agents within 30 minutes of delay confirmation.
value.scope: Applies to all flight bookings created by travel agent partners on the B2B platform that experience a confirmed flight schedule delay exceeding three hours.
prerequisites: Access to the internal booking management system and flight monitoring feed.
Access to the Global Distribution System (GDS) and airline trade helpdesk communication channels.
Access to agent notification templates and communication logs.

procedure.instruction: Filter the internal booking management system by the delayed flight number and date to extract all active Passenger Name Records (PNRs) and their associated travel agent contact details.
procedure.expected_result: A complete list of affected PNRs and matching travel agent contact records is generated.

procedure.instruction: Review each identified PNR to check for onward connecting flights, hotel bookings, or ground transfers within the same or linked itineraries.
procedure.expected_result: All PNRs with downstream connection risks or multi-segment impacts are identified and tagged as high priority.

procedure.instruction: Contact the operating airline's trade desk or consult the published trade disruption policy to obtain official rebooking options, fee waivers, or involuntary refund guidelines.
procedure.expected_result: Clear rebooking alternatives, available flight availability, and fee waiver rules are confirmed and documented for the incident.

procedure.instruction: Send the standard delay notification to each affected travel agent, specifying the delay duration, impact on onward connections, available alternative flights, and refund policies.
procedure.expected_result: Written notification email sent to travel agents within 30 minutes of delay confirmation, with delivery timestamp recorded.

procedure.instruction: Log the communication timestamp, agent choices, and updated itinerary details in the internal PNR file.
procedure.expected_result: Internal system updated with complete audit trail and status of agent instructions.

decision_points.question: Does the affected traveller have an onward connecting flight or downstream booking at risk of being missed?
decision_points.if_yes: Flag the PNR as High Priority, evaluate alternative full-route itineraries, and include connection rebooking options in the agent notice.
decision_points.if_no: Process the PNR under standard delay handling for point-to-point travel options.

decision_points.question: Has the airline issued an explicit trade waiver policy covering involuntary changes and fee waivers for this delay?
decision_points.if_yes: Apply the waiver policy conditions directly when outlining options to the travel agent.
decision_points.if_no: Submit an urgent trade desk authorization request while providing the agent standard fare rule options with a waiver-pending note.

exceptions.situation: Airline trade desk does not respond within 15 minutes of initial request.
exceptions.action: Dispatch preliminary delay notification to travel agents stating available scheduled alternatives and noting that final carrier waiver approval is pending, then re-send urgent request to trade desk.

exceptions.situation: The operating airline rebooks the traveller at the airport before the travel agent responds.
exceptions.action: Sync PNR from GDS to pull updated carrier flight segments, update internal system, and notify travel agent of the carrier-executed rebooking details.

exceptions.situation: No direct or connecting alternative flights are available on the same travel date.
exceptions.action: Provide travel agent options for next-day flights with partner airlines under interline agreements, or present full involuntary refund details.

escalation_rules.trigger: Airline trade desk fails to provide waiver or rebooking approval within 20 minutes of flight delay alert.
Travel agent partner demands commercial compensation or carrier policy exception outside standard agent guidelines.

checklist: Confirmed flight delay duration exceeds 3 hours on flight tracking feed.
Extracted full list of affected PNRs and corresponding travel agent contacts.
Evaluated all itineraries for onward flight connections and land arrangements.
Retrieved official airline trade waiver policy and alternative flight options.
Dispatched standardized delay and option email to all travel agents within 30 minutes.
Logged dispatch time and agent responses in internal booking records.

kpis.name: Travel Agent Notification Time SLA
kpis.target: 100% of affected agents notified within 30 minutes of delay confirmation
kpis.how_measured: Difference between confirmed delay timestamp in system and notification dispatch timestamp in CRM.

kpis.name: Onward Connection Protection Rate
kpis.target: 100% of affected connecting itineraries assessed and offered alternative routes
kpis.how_measured: Audit of high-priority PNR logs comparing total missed connections to documented rebooking options provided to agents.

risks.description: Travellers receive direct airline SMS alerts before their travel agent is informed by the B2B team, leading to agent dissatisfaction.
risks.mitigation: Strict adherence to the 30-minute notification workflow with prioritized processing of high-impact delays.

risks.description: Missed identification of onward connecting segments booked across separate PNRs.
risks.mitigation: Perform agent customer history cross-reference search during Step 2 to locate linked single-passenger bookings.

improvement_suggestions: Integrate automated flight delay alerts into the booking system to automatically flag affected PNRs and generate agent contact lists.
Develop automated email generation for flight delay options that pre-fills alternative flight itineraries directly from GDS availability.
